newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian shares end lower led by top two banks.
newsitem.headline: Colombian shares end lower led by top two banks.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 17 Reuter - Colombian stocks ended mostly lower for the second straight day as shares in the country's two top banks fell under selling pressure, brokers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index shed 0.38 percent to close at 17,192.56 on above-average volume of more than 18 billion pesos, most of it stemming from a large cross-trade in shares of Banco Industrial Colombiano. The bank, financial arm of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, closed unchanged at 3,750 per share.
Bogota's closed down 0.35 percent, ending the day at 1,125.38 on lackluster volume of l.1 billion pesos.

Movers were led by Banco Ganadero and Banco de Colombia, the country's two biggest commercial banks in terms of assets. Banco de Colombia fell 1.96 percent to a new low for the year of 400 pesos per share in Bogota on what dealers described as continuing concerns and frustration over delays in its strategic alliance with Spain's Banco Central Hispano.
"No clear message has been given to Banco de Colombia shareholders about its negotiations with Banco Central Hispano," one Medellin-based broker said. "People are getting tired of this situation."
Ganadero slipped 1.42 percent to close at 345 pesos per share, falling on what brokers called mostly speculative profit-taking since there was no news to explain the downward move.
Gains were led by Compania Suramericana de Seguros, centerpiece of the diversified Sindicato Antioqueno group. It rose 1.31 percent to end at 26,340 pesos a share in Medellin on foreign fund buying.
Brewer Bavaria, also buoyed by foreign fund interest, ended up 0.62 percent at 8,000 pesos per share.
